title: Candy Corn Bag

adjustment.analysis: No events, no price change, and no promotion in the target week. The baseline already reflects recent seasonal trends (back-to-school season ending in late August) and the Labor Day holiday effect (Sep 7) was already captured. The classical uplift model's suggestion of x1.0 is appropriate. No driver justifies an adjustment. The noise-adjusted effect of past promotions is x1.48, but the discount was only 10% and the week after a promotion shows no pull-forward. Confidence is high as the forecast is stable and no new drivers exist.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-80% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
